title: Why big clocks keep better time

data.source: The rotor of MATHEMATICS.md R4 in four settings (independent, alternating, slow noise, seed memory), 300 runs each.

prediction: Grouping M occasions shrinks the relative spread by 1/sqrt(M) only when the gaps are independent; the printed alternating rotor is steadier than that, slow noise is looser, seed memory shifts it, and the textbook correction for correlated gaps gives the right answer in every case.
baseline: The central limit theorem, with the long-run variance correction for correlated terms.
why: P1, P2, P3 and P5 held. P4 missed: seed memory at the suggested strength moved the spread by less than I predicted. The 1/sqrt(M) rule in the wider notes is the central limit theorem for independent gaps and fails, as that theorem says it must, when gaps remember each other. Nothing is left over for CRR.
